Subject: Audit cutover: end date inclusivity & point-in-time evidence

Hi Emily / AuditOps team,

Thanks for sending the draft SOC 2 Type II report listing the period Jan 1, 2026 - Jun 30, 2026. We have a couple of practical evidence-capture questions as our customer-facing teams prepare exports: 

1) End-date inclusivity: does the report treat Jun 30, 2026 as inclusive through the end of that calendar day? If so, which timezone should we interpret (report-stated timezone, customer local time, or UTC) when we pull per-customer logs?

2) Point-in-time / cutover guidance: some of our telemetry is captured as rolling snapshots and we also have ingestion timestamps that cross midnight (e.g., events with server_ts at 2026-06-30T00:12:23Z). For customers onboarded mid-June, do you accept evidence showing activity through Jun 30 at 23:59:59 (server_ts) or do you require a snapshot timestamp exactly at 00:00 to validate presence/absence?

Attached a small sample-log-snippet.csv to show the kinds of timestamps we pull. Also copy Neha (internal compliance) and looping in Marissa (audit lead) for visibility.

If helpful, we can schedule a short call to align on what exact fields/timezones you need for evidence exports.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample-log-snippet.csv (CSV, 14 KB)
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@fintechcorp.com>

Cc: AuditOps <audits@big4audit.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Audit cutover: end date inclusivity & point-in-time evidence

Hi Priyom — thanks for the clear questions and the sample. Quick answers: 

1) End-date inclusivity: Jun 30 is inclusive to the end of the calendar day. If the report header specifies a timezone (we typically use PST for North American engagements), use that timezone. If no timezone is explicit in the report, assume UTC for evidence cutoffs.

2) Point-in-time evidence: we accept either (a) a snapshot taken at or very near the end of day (e.g., 23:59:xx in the report timezone) that demonstrates presence/absence, or (b) an event-level export where server_ts shows timestamps up to 23:59:59 of Jun 30 in the report timezone. We do not require a snapshot taken exactly at 00:00 unless your internal process documents that as the system snapshot time. The key is that the timestamps are consistent and you can show how the snapshot or export was produced. 

Bridge letters: for situations where there is ambiguity around timezone conversions or partial-day onboarding, we can issue a short bridge letter to state how we interpreted cutoffs for the report. I'm attaching a bridge-letter-template.docx you can adapt.

If you want to run a quick example from your dataset over us, we can validate the extract. Happy to hop on a 20-min call — I pasted a calendar slot below.

Cheers,
Emily Chen
Senior Audit Manager
FinTechCorp Audit Services

Attachments: bridge-letter-template.docx (DOCX, 28 KB)

Hi Emily — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups: 

• We use UTC internally for most server_ts but our customer dashboards are in PT. To be explicit, if the report is PST and you say inclusive to 23:59 PST, that maps to 06:59 UTC the following day — is that exactly how you prefer we present the evidence (i.e., convert all server_ts to the report timezone and include a note about conversion)?

• For rolling snapshots: we capture a daily snapshot job that runs at 00:05 UTC (so technically a few minutes after midnight). Would a snapshot job timestamped 2026-07-01T00:05:10Z that claims to reflect state as of 2026-06-30 23:59:59 PST be acceptable if we supply a short explanation of the job timing and the mapping?

We have a few customers who changed retention toggles on Jun 30 evening; auditors want to know which retention setting applied at cutover. Would you prefer we provide per-customer ingestion_time + retention_flag history for the range Jun 28–Jul 02?

If a short call is easiest, Neha and Marissa are available this afternoon — suggested windows: 1:00–1:30 PM PT or 3:00–3:30 PM PT.
